title: Player router placement and director growth enforce different spacing metrics despite the 'shared' E31 rule
evidence:
+// Router placement validity: inside the map grid and clear of every live node
+// by the growth separation distance (E31's spacing rule, shared so the map
+// never gets two nodes on top of each other regardless of who placed them).
...
+	sep2 := bal.growth_min_dist_tiles * bal.growth_min_dist_tiles
+		d := t.node_pos[i] - pos
+		if d[0]*d[0] + d[1]*d[1] < sep2 { return false }
...
+		d := manhattan(t.node_pos[i], cand)
+		if d < bal.growth_min_dist_tiles { return false }
detail: Growth spawns enforce Manhattan separation; player router placement enforces Euclidean, though the comment calls E31's rule 'shared'. A node growth may spawn (Manhattan-ok, Euclidean-too-close) could never be player-placed — two different spacing rules.
recommended_fix: Make both paths use one metric (Manhattan, matching min_dist_ok) or both Euclidean; centralize in a shared spacing proc so growth and placement can't drift.

title: Single surge_active flag is cleared by the first set-piece resolution while other pieces remain active
evidence:
+		if !d.triggered[i] && set_piece_active(sp, tick) {
+			d.triggered[i] = true
+			c.surge_active = true
...
+		if d.triggered[i] && !d.resolved[i] && tick >= sp.start_tick + sp.duration_ticks {
+			d.resolved[i] = true
+			c.surge_active = false
detail: surge_active is a single bool but set pieces are per-index. When overlapping pieces exist, the first resolution sets surge_active=false while another piece is still active; snapshot surge_active and Ev_Crisis_Resolved then contradict plan-based health surge windows.
recommended_fix: Derive surge_active from the plan (len(active set pieces) > 0) like health_update does, or count active/triggered pieces and only clear when none remain.

title: demand_weight parsed from JSON but never consumed; spawn path hardcodes weight 1
evidence:
+	demand_weight: i32,
...
+			append(weights, 1) // demand_weight is uniform in the PROTO roster
...
+			de.demand_weight = jint(eo, "demand_weight", 1)
...
+			pt.demand_weight = jint(eo, "demand_weight", 1)
detail: Demand_Entry and Packet_Type both parse demand_weight from JSON, but the spawn path hardcodes weight 1 ('uniform in the PROTO roster'). Any non-uniform roster silently ignores the parsed field — the data model and the sim disagree.
recommended_fix: Use entry.demand_weight when building src_w/dst_w (or delete the fields and the JSON keys so the format cannot promise what the sim ignores).

title: route_entry_node bails on tombstoned completed edges while current_node walks through them — inconsistent walkers
evidence:
+		ps, ok := t.pipe_by_id[p.route[i]] // id->slot persists after tombstone
+		if !ok { return node }
...
+		ps, ok := pipe_slot(t, p.route[i])
+		if !ok { return node }
...
+	s, ok := t.pipe_by_id[id]
+	return s, ok && t.pipe_alive[s]
detail: current_node walks tombstoned completed edges via pipe_by_id (documented), but route_entry_node uses pipe_slot, which requires liveness, and bails early. After an E27 demolish behind an in-flight packet, snapshot positions/direction flip wrong and the two walkers disagree.
recommended_fix: Make route_entry_node use t.pipe_by_id like current_node (endpoint data persists), and add a test: demolish a pipe behind an in-flight packet, then check packet_edge_pos.

title: pick_dst allocates per spawned packet with the run allocator in the hot path, contradicting the no-churn scratch convention
evidence:
+	cand: [dynamic]u32
+	cand_w: [dynamic]i32
+	defer delete(cand)
+	defer delete(cand_w)
...
+	// per-tick scratch (persistent — no per-tick allocator churn)
detail: pick_dst allocates two dynamic arrays per spawned packet via context.allocator (set to the run arena by step), while Flow_State's persistent scratch fields exist to avoid per-tick churn. On an arena, delete is a no-op: memory grows per spawn.
recommended_fix: Reuse the existing sc_dst_ids/sc_dst_w scratch: filter in place or add a small persistent dst-filter buffer; never allocate per packet in the run arena.

title: Explicit run allocator not threaded into flow_init/director_init_growth — run state splits across two allocators
evidence:
+	state.inventory = Inventory{
+		links = make([]i32, len(cat.pipe_tiers), allocator),
...
+	flow_init(&state.flow, cat)
...
+	director_init_growth(&state.director, &state.rng, &cat.balance)
...
+flow_init :: proc(f: ^Flow_State, cat: ^Catalogs, allocator := context.allocator) {
...
+	// NOTE: never assigns context.allocator — the core must not mutate the
+	// caller's context (allocator mixing = heap aborts; r1 lesson)
detail: run_init accepts an explicit run allocator and inventory uses it, but flow_init and director_init_growth default to context.allocator. Run state splits across two allocators — the mixing the file's own NOTE says causes heap aborts — and run_destroy frees neither side.
recommended_fix: Thread state.allocator into flow_init and director_init_growth (and restore context.allocator in catalogs_load, which also assigns it without restoring).

title: Neutral (uptime -1) window during an open breach drains the meter at max rate, contradicting 'no breach, no credit'
evidence:
+	if recent_uptime < 0 {
+		// neutral: no breach, no credit — but an open episode stays open
...
+			severity := bal.win_uptime_pct - recent_uptime
+			drain := clamp(severity / 10, 1, bal.meter_drain_per_tick_max)
detail: During an open breach episode, a neutral (uptime -1) window computes severity = win_uptime_pct - (-1), draining the meter at the maximum per-tick rate while the comment says neutral traffic gives 'no breach, no credit' — the drain violates that.
recommended_fix: Treat uptime -1 as non-breaching for drain purposes: skip drain while neutral (keep the band open per E30, but don't drain with a bogus severity).

title: Fail-fast contract not implemented: unknown fields never rejected, non-object entries silently skipped
evidence:
+// catalog.odin — data-driven content catalogs (ODN-5). JSON single source,
+// loaded once, fail-fast validated (unknown fields, out-of-range values,
+// cross-reference errors abort with a named error), read-only after load.
...
+			eo := ev.(json.Object) or_continue
detail: Header promises fail-fast on 'unknown fields, out-of-range values', but no unknown-field detection exists and non-object entries are silently skipped via or_continue. A catalog with garbage entries partially loads instead of aborting with a named error.
recommended_fix: Reject unknown keys per entry and error on non-object entries (return Catalog_Error with the entry index) so the loader matches its documented fail-fast contract.

title: Numeric fields unvalidated: negative at_tick/start_tick wrap via u64(i32); volume/multiplier unchecked; i64->i32 truncation
evidence:
+				g.at_tick = u64(jint(go, "at_tick", 0))
...
+				sp.start_tick = u64(jint(so, "start_tick", 0))
...
+	#partial switch x in v {
+	case json.Integer: return i32(x), true
+	case json.Float:   return i32(x), true
+	}
detail: Fail-fast claim aside, negative at_tick/start_tick wrap via u64(i32) into huge values (grants/forecasts silently never fire), volume/multiplier have no range check, and jcount/jint truncate i64->i32.
recommended_fix: Validate: at_tick/start_tick >= 0, volume > 0, multiplier >= 1 (error with named rule), and range-check json.Integer before narrowing.

title: w_i64 defined but never called anywhere in the diff
detail: w_i64 is defined but no call site exists in the diff — state_writer and log_write never use it. If no other chunk consumes it, it is dead code.
recommended_fix: Delete w_i64, or add a caller if a planned writer (e.g., a future state reader) needs it.

title: growth_pool serialized without a length prefix, violating the 'lengths-not-capacities' format claim
evidence:
+	for v in d.growth_pool { w_i32(&w, v[0]); w_i32(&w, v[1]) }
...
+// serialize.odin — the canonical serialized form (ODN-11/T1). Field-wise
+// little-endian, lengths-not-capacities, no padding, no pointers — INCLUDING
detail: Header claims the format is 'lengths-not-capacities', but growth_pool is written with no length prefix, unlike every other dynamic array (node_health, roll windows, event stream all write lengths). A reader cannot parse state_dump without the catalog.
recommended_fix: Write u32(len(d.growth_pool)) before the entries (and pin it in the replay-equality test by making the reader round-trip the dump).

title: run.odin step-order header names topology_apply_all but the body applies commands one-by-one via topology_apply_edit
evidence:
+//   1. topology_apply_all (replay/tooling commands; live edits already landed
+//      via the ODN-2 fast-path)
...
+			_, err := topology_apply_edit(&state.topology, cmd, state.catalogs, state.inventory, cmd.apply_tick)
detail: run.odin's pinned step-order header says step applies replay via 'topology_apply_all', but the body loops topology_apply_edit per command, explicitly rejecting the atomic batch. One of the two is stale; readers of the header will misread replay semantics.
recommended_fix: Update the step-order comment to name topology_apply_edit/in-order application, or actually route replay commands through topology_apply_all.

title: Cmd_Set_Pipe_Priority comment documents "" as neutral but the field is i32 with -1 as neutral
evidence:
+// The PROTO QoS surface (GDD § M2 'priority emphasis' dial): "" = neutral
+// (all classes ride Standard), else the named class rides Express and the
+// others ride Best on this pipe.
...
+	priority:     i32, // class index, or -1 for neutral
detail: The command comment documents the neutral priority as "" (empty string) but the field is i32 with -1 as neutral. A leftover from a string-based design; the two cannot both be right.
recommended_fix: Update the comment to '-1 = neutral', matching the field type and qos.effective_lane's checks.

title: run_destroy frees only the two lookup maps; all other run-owned allocations are leaked
detail: run_destroy deletes only the two lookup maps. flow_init's dynamic arrays, director flags, growth_pool, inventory slices, events, and action_log are never freed — with a general allocator the run leaks everything except the maps.
recommended_fix: Free all run-owned allocations in run_destroy (or document that the caller must tear down the run arena and drop the function).

title: Severance reroute resets edge_idx/progress_units but not vis_q8 — rerouted packets visually teleport
evidence:
+		cur := current_node(p, t)
+		compute_route(f, t, cur, p.dst, p)
+		p.edge_idx = 0
+		p.progress_units = 0
detail: Severance reroute resets edge_idx and progress_units but not vis_q8, so a rerouted packet's visual fraction is walked over the new route — packet_edge_pos can fall through to 'return 0, 0, p.dst', teleporting the dot to the destination.
recommended_fix: Reset p.vis_q8 (e.g., spawn-phase offset) after reroute so the visual walk restarts on the new route, and cover it in a reroute test.
